Good to know before you apply

  • One BUS grant per property — you can't claim twice for the same home.
  • No EPC hurdle: you no longer need an EPC with no outstanding insulation recommendations to apply for BUS.
  • MCS-certified installer required for BUS — the installer applies for the grant on your behalf.
  • ECO4 is different: it's based on household eligibility and property efficiency, and it closes on 31 December 2026.
⏰ ECO4 ends 31 Dec 2026 · BUS uplift to 31 Mar 2027

Every grant, in detail

What each scheme pays, who qualifies, and how to apply — the same detail you'd find on a dedicated page for each grant. Figures checked against GOV.UK, Ofgem and HMRC, updated October 2026.

Grant · England & Wales

Boiler Upgrade Scheme

The main heat pump grant. You get £7,500 off an air source or ground source heat pump — and £9,000 if your home is heated by oil or LPG with no mains gas connection, for installs from 21 July 2026 to 31 March 2027. There's no income test, and since 28 April 2026 you no longer need an EPC with no outstanding insulation recommendations.

  • £7,500 — air source and ground source heat pumps
  • £9,000 — oil/LPG off-gas homes, to 31 March 2027
  • £5,000 — biomass boilers
  • £2,500 — air-to-air heat pumps, in law from 28 April 2026 but not claimable until MCS certifies installers for them
  • One grant per property; new builds don't qualify
  • Your MCS-certified installer applies to Ofgem for the voucher on your behalf

A typical air source heat pump install costs £10,000–£15,000 before the grant, so most homeowners pay £2,500–£7,500 after it.

Grant · England, Scotland & Wales · Ends 31 Dec 2026

ECO4 Scheme

ECO4 is an obligation on the big energy suppliers, administered by Ofgem. It funds a whole-house package of insulation and heating upgrades for low-income homes — usually fully funded, though a top-up is sometimes asked for. It ends on 31 December 2026 and all work must be finished by then; there is no ECO5.

  • You generally need a means-tested benefit (Universal Credit, Pension Credit, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Income Support or Housing Benefit) and an EPC rating of D–G
  • Owner-occupiers, and tenants with their landlord's permission
  • No benefit? Your council's LA Flex route can still qualify some households
  • Typical savings: loft insulation ~£310/yr, cavity wall ~£395/yr, solid wall ~£505/yr, heating and solar measures £200–£600/yr
  • You apply through an approved installer, not GOV.UK; a typical process takes 4–8 weeks

When ECO4 ends, the routes that remain are the Warm Homes: Local Grant in England, Warmer Homes Scotland and Nest in Wales — plus the Boiler Upgrade Scheme for heat pumps.

Grant · England · Part of the Warm Homes Plan

Warm Homes: Local Grant

A £500m, council-delivered scheme running to March 2028, and the main part of the wider Warm Homes Plan. It pays for a survey-led package — insulation, an air source heat pump, smart controls and solar — at no cost to eligible owner-occupiers.

  • Qualify one of three ways: household income of £36,000 a year or less, a means-tested benefit, or a home in a low-income (IMD decile 1–2) postcode
  • Your home needs an EPC rating of D–G and must be privately owned — social housing isn't covered
  • Tenants pay nothing; landlords get one home fully funded, then pay 50% for further homes
  • Apply via GOV.UK; your council usually contacts you within 10 working days
  • Be aware: many councils are already full for 2026/27, and you should never pay anyone upfront for this grant

Tax relief · UK-wide · To 31 Mar 2027

VAT Relief — 0% VAT

Energy-saving materials installed in your home are charged at 0% VAT until 31 March 2027, when the rate goes up to 5%. There's nothing to apply for — your installer applies it on the quote. It covers solar panels, heat pumps, insulation and battery storage (standalone batteries included since February 2024), but not DIY or shop-bought kits, which are charged at 20%.

  • A £6,000 solar install saves £1,200 in VAT
  • A £10,000 heat pump install saves £2,000
  • A £5,000 battery saves £1,000
  • It stacks with other help — you can combine it with ECO4, the Boiler Upgrade Scheme and LA Flex

Verified against HMRC VAT Notice 708/6.

Upgrades, costs and grants

Each upgrade on its own page's worth of detail: what it costs, what it saves, and which grant helps pay for it.

Service · Solar

Solar Panels

Rooftop solar panels generate electricity you use for free, and you're paid for what you export through the Smart Export Guarantee (SEG), at roughly 3–15p per kWh depending on supplier. A typical 4kW system makes about 3,400 kWh a year. Installers must be MCS-certified, and rooftop solar is usually permitted development — no planning permission for most homes.

  • 3kW system: £4,500–£6,000 · 4kW: £6,600–£7,800 · 6kW: £8,000–£12,000
  • A 4kW system is worth about £630–£760 a year, with a typical payback of 9–12 years
  • Adding a battery costs roughly £4,000–£8,000 more
  • There's no universal free solar grant: free solar only comes as part of an ECO4, LA Flex or Warm Homes: Local Grant package for eligible low-income homes with EPC D–G
  • Everyone else still gets 0% VAT until 31 March 2027, plus SEG export payments

Service · Heating

Heat Pumps

An air source heat pump heats your home and hot water using electricity far more efficiently than a boiler. The median install cost £12,826 in July–September 2026 — around £5,326 after the £7,500 Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant, or around £3,826 after the £9,000 off-gas rate. Fitting one usually takes 2–3 days.

  • Running cost around £895 a year at a typical efficiency (SCOP 3.0), versus about £1,065 for a gas boiler at the October–December 2026 price cap
  • Against oil, savings can reach ~£770 a year; against LPG ~£550 a year
  • Ground source heat pumps cost more — a median of about £26,500, or ~£19,000 after the grant
  • The grant has no income test, and your MCS installer claims it for you

Service · Insulation

Insulation

Often the cheapest upgrade and the quickest to pay back — and the one most grants fund in full. The live routes are ECO4 (to 31 December 2026), LA Flex through your council, and the Warm Homes: Local Grant (to March 2028). The Great British Insulation Scheme closed on 31 March 2026. Most schemes need an EPC rating of D–G.

  • Loft insulation: saves up to ~£590 a year, fitted in 2–4 hours
  • Cavity wall insulation: ~£395 a year, fitted in 2–3 hours
  • Solid wall insulation: ~£225–£475 a year, takes 1–4 weeks
  • Underfloor insulation: up to ~£100 a year
  • Room-in-roof and park home insulation are also covered by some schemes

Service · Storage

Battery Storage

A home battery stores spare solar power — or cheap off-peak electricity — for when you need it. Sizes typically run 5–15kWh, with around 10kWh suiting most homes, and a lifespan of roughly 10–12 years. Batteries are 0% VAT until 31 March 2027, whether fitted with panels or on their own.

  • Costs run £1,500–£10,000; about £4,600 for a 5kWh battery (Energy Saving Trust)
  • In worked examples, a 10kWh battery saves £343–£640 a year
  • Straight about the downside: on a flat tariff with no solar, a battery can lose money — it earns its keep paired with solar or a time-of-use tariff

Service · EV Charging

EV Charger Grants

The EV chargepoint grant takes up to £500 — 75% of the cost — off a home charger, but it's aimed at renters and flat owners with private off-street parking. If you own a house with a driveway, you're generally not eligible for the home grant. Residential landlords can get up to £500 per socket. All of the open home grants end on 31 March 2027, and the installer must be OZEV-approved.

  • A 7kW smart charger typically costs £900–£1,300 installed — £400–£800 after the grant if you're eligible
  • Charging at home off-peak (around 7–10p/kWh) costs roughly £300 a year for 10,000 miles, versus about £1,800 in petrol
  • Pairing solar with an EV can save £1,500–£2,500 a year combined

What is
HeatFund?

An independent guide to upgrading your home: which upgrades are worth it, what they cost, and every grant that can help. We're not the government's Great British Energy (gbe.gov.uk), and we're not an energy supplier.

More about us
UK energy grants available in 2026 include the Boiler Upgrade Scheme (£7,500 towards a heat pump in England and Wales, or £9,000 for an air or ground source heat pump in oil- or LPG-heated homes with no mains gas until 31 March 2027), the Warm Homes: Local Grant, 0% VAT until 31 March 2027, the Warm Home Discount (£150 off electricity bills) and ECO4, which closes on 31 December 2026. Scotland has Home Energy Scotland and Warmer Homes Scotland, and Wales has Nest.

One installer, never a marketplace

Your details go to one suitable installer that covers your area, and only when you ask for a quote. Your enquiry is not passed to anyone else.

Checked against the source

Grant figures are checked against GOV.UK, Ofgem and the Scottish and Welsh schemes, and each guide shows when.

Certified installers only

Before we introduce anyone, we check their MCS registration for solar, batteries and heat pumps, or TrustMark for insulation.

Straight about costs

Grants don't cover everything. When they don't, we say so and show what the upgrade really costs.
